title: Book: The Millionaire Next Door — Thomas Stanley and William Danko (1996)
publisher: Artha Kavach original summary of a book's ideas (paraphrase, not a quotation; the author's opinion, not settled fact) — pending manual verification
text: Thomas Stanley and William Danko surveyed wealthy households in the US and found that many were not flashy: they lived below their means, budgeted, invested steadily, and often ran ordinary businesses. They distinguish 'prodigious accumulators of wealth' (people whose net worth is much higher than expected for their income) from 'under-accumulators' (high earners with low net worth because they spend what they make). The message is that wealth is what you keep and invest, not what you earn or display, and that giving adult children large handouts can undermine their own habits. Limits: the data is from US households in the 1990s, the 'average' findings hide a lot of variety, and later research has questioned some conclusions; the habit lessons still hold.
